INTEGRATED SCIENCE — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Burning crop residue every week
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Removing all vegetation

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

4. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reproduction in plants? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reproduction in plants.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Reproduction in plants.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reproduction in plants.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reproduction in plants.

6. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. A chemical reaction forming ash
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.

9. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

10. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Nitrogen gas only
   C. Only water vapour
   D. Glucose and oxygen

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Structure of the atom? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Structure of the atom.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Structure of the atom.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Structure of the atom.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Structure of the atom.

14. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Paper burning to ash
   D. Milk souring

15. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. newton (N)
   C. watt (W)
   D. pascal (Pa)

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Curved mirrors? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Curved mirrors.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Curved mirrors.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Curved mirrors.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Curved mirrors.

17. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Primary consumers only
   B. Tertiary consumers
   C. Decomposers only
   D. Producers

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
18. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reproduction in plants and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain The Interdependence of Life and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

23. In three clear sentences, explain Curved mirrors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

24. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

25. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
